draft.title: Style across a whole text
card: A writer's style is the pattern of choices that runs through a whole text. It is not one clever line. It is what the writer keeps doing.
Style can include sentence rhythm, imagery, tone, word choice and irony. For example, a writer might use short, blunt sentences in every chapter, or keep returning to images of water.
A single technique shows a choice. A repeated technique shows a pattern. A pattern is the evidence that a choice is part of the writer's style.
Studying style means asking what the pattern does for the reader. It shows how the whole text builds its meaning, such as a mood of tension or a sense of distance.
draft.remember: Style is a pattern of choices. Track it across the text and ask what it does.

a.q: Which of these best describes a writer's style?
opts: A pattern of choices that runs through a text
The most striking technique in the opening chapter
The plot events that happen in the final scene
The main theme that the writer wants to teach
a.why: Style is about repeated choices across a whole text, such as rhythm or imagery. One striking technique is only a single choice, so it does not show a style by itself.
a.clue: Think about what the writer keeps doing, not what they do once.

b.q: Priya notices that a novel uses a cold, flat tone in every chapter, and she uses this to explain the narrator's distance from others. Why is this a study of style?
opts: She tracks a repeated choice and links it to meaning
She finds one tone and names it in a single scene
She retells the plot and adds her opinion of the narrator
She compares the narrator with a person she knows
b.why: Priya follows a pattern across the whole text and explains what it does for meaning. Naming a technique in one scene is tempting, but it shows only one choice, not a pattern.
b.clue: Look for the option that mentions both a pattern and its effect.

a.best: A pattern of choices that runs through a text

b.best: She tracks a repeated choice and links it to meaning

proposal.title: Style across a whole text
card: A writer's style is the pattern of choices that runs through a whole text. It is not one clever line. It is what the writer keeps doing.

Style is about how a text is written, not what happens in it or what it is about. It can include sentence rhythm, imagery, tone, word choice and irony, such as short, blunt sentences in every chapter or recurring images of water.
A single technique shows one choice. A repeated technique shows a pattern. A pattern is the evidence that a choice is part of the writer's style.
Studying style means asking what the pattern does for the reader. It shows how the whole text builds its meaning, such as a mood of tension or a sense of distance.
proposal.remember: Spot the pattern, then explain what it does for meaning.

a.q: A student is writing about a novel. Which observation is evidence of the writer's style?
opts: Short, blunt sentences recur whenever the narrator is afraid
A striking metaphor of a locked door opens the last chapter
The narrator slowly grows braver as the story unfolds
The novel explores the cost of living in fear
a.why: Short sentences that keep returning at moments of fear are a repeated choice about how the text is written, so they form a pattern. The locked door metaphor is tempting, but it is one choice in one place. The narrator's growth is what happens, and fear is what the novel is about.
a.clue: Separate how the novel is written from what happens in it.

b.q: Priya notices that a novel uses a cold, flat tone in every chapter, and she uses this to explain the narrator's distance from others. Why is this a study of style?
opts: She tracks a repeated choice and links it to meaning
She counts the chapters in which the cold tone appears
She names the cold tone she finds in one main scene
She retells the plot to show how distant the narrator is
b.why: Priya follows the cold tone across the whole novel and explains what it does: it builds the narrator's distance. Counting the chapters is tempting, but it only finds the pattern without asking what it does for the reader.
b.clue: Spotting a choice is only the first step.
